places.name: Andalen Plantation

why.founding: A Dres saltrice enterprise with a great house, a drying floor, a counting room and a labour row, abandoned at the secession when the people who worked it stopped and the family who owned it did not come back.
why.siteAdvantages: Prime saltrice ground on slack water with a private landing. It still failed.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing occupies the house. The fields are worked by the people from the rows down the road, who take the crop and will not enter the buildings.
why.pressures: The house is intact and unlooted, which after two centuries means somebody is maintaining an arrangement rather than a building; nobody will say who.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be occupied within a month if the field-holders decided the taboo was over. The house is worth more than the whole village.

places.name: Buried Blades
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: In 1E 2836 the Argonians stopped fighting the Blackwater War overnight, and in the north they buried the proof: a whole district's weapons oiled, wrapped and put in one pit, so that stopping could not easily be undone.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry gravel lens under a low rise, chosen because it drains. That is why the contents are still recognisable.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody guards it. Four villages know where it is and have known for sixteen hundred years, and the knowledge is transmitted as a warning rather than as an asset.
why.pressures: An-Xileel interest in the province's armament has made the pit's existence newly awkward, and one of the four villages has started asking what the others would do.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would change the north's politics in a week if it were opened. Four villages have not opened it.

hardConstraints: a dry gravel lens under a rise

places.name: Hutan-Tzel
places.whySiteWon: spring head in firm lowland (danger band 2), 50 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: An old tribal village on the Panther River where it drains into its basin, holding the western approach to the north. It has its own tribe, its own elder naheesh, and a xanmeer, Xal Irasotl, close enough to be the tribe's charge rather than its neighbour.
why.siteAdvantages: The basin edge: still water for the village, running water for the trip downstream, and a rock shelf the flood never takes. The Imperial maps call it Rockguard for that shelf.

why.founding: Stormhold built a stone causeway to Bogmother because the pilgrimage could not wait on the season.
why.siteAdvantages: The shortest line of shallow bog between the city's south gate and the sacred ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The city maintains it as a civic duty; the maintenance gang is a hereditary office with a bad reputation.
why.pressures: It is stone, which since the Duskfall counts as a moral compromise; the pilgrimage is the only reason the compromise is tolerated.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced with timber if it ever failed completely, which the caretakers would prefer and the city would not.

hardConstraints: shallow bog between two fixed points

why.founding: The Tear road is one of the province's two roads out, and a road to Morrowind needs a last stage on the Argonian side.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the road leaves the marsh for the pass, the last place with fodder, water and level ground.
why.occupantsMotive: The stage is run by a family who take payment in both coin and salt and prefer salt.
why.pressures: Dunmer caravans and Argonian porters use the same yard and keep to opposite sides of it.

places.name: Tearmouth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 2), 612 m from the nearest route; no free 'natural-harbour' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on region, hinterland, danger.

why.founding: Where the north river meets navigable water, cargo has to change hulls; a two-culture port grew at the transfer point, Argonian on the water and Dunmer on the bank, and has been arguing about which half is the port ever since.
why.siteAdvantages: The head of deep-draught navigation: below it a keeled hull can float, above it only shallow craft, and no engineering has ever changed that.
why.occupantsMotive: Transfer fees, warehousing, a customs presence run out of Thorn with two clerks, and a great deal of business that the two clerks are not shown.
why.pressures: Both halves of the town want the customs house on the other side of the water; the Thorn road wants a bridge; and the whole place empties for six weeks when the river runs too hard to transfer at all.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would lose half its trade to a deeper channel and all of it to a bridge. It has resisted both for a century.

places.hook: Where cargo changes hulls: two half-towns, one customs house and any berth you like if you ask the right half.

places.name: Ten-Maur-Wolk
places.whySiteWon: saddle in upland hills (danger band 3), 1132 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on landform, region, remote.

why.founding: A temple to Boethiah and Vaermina raised by Dunmer dissidents who fled the Tribunal, and abandoned by them. The Third Empire's surveyors renamed it Tenmar Wall on their maps; the north never adopted the name, and the market that carries the shortened form grew half a morning's walk away, on the road, which is as close as anyone wanted to build.
why.siteAdvantages: Off the road and out of the way, in a hollow the tracks curve around, which is why everyone in the north knows of it and nobody goes to it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The marker posts around it are maintained.
why.pressures: The market town that borrowed its name lives off the road and pretends the ruin is somebody else's business; the second atrocity on this ground is the Dres slave road that ran past the district, not anything the dissidents built.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would draw a cult within a year if the markers ever stopped being renewed.

hardConstraints: off every route, in ground that carries no track
places.hook: A Daedric shrine the north has ringed with new white posts and will not discuss.

places.name: Ten-Thousand-Nests
places.whySiteWon: islet in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 695 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A stand of dead trees in shallow water where the north's wading birds nest in numbers that make the stand uninhabitable and the ground beneath it the richest fertiliser source in the region.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead standing timber over water: no predator route in, no need for the birds to leave, and forty years of guano under it.
why.occupantsMotive: The villages take guano for the terraces in one licensed month and stay away for eleven, an arrangement enforced by the smell as much as by anyone.
why.pressures: The saltrice growers want more than one month; the villages that eat the eggs want none at all; the stand itself is rotting and falling tree by tree.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would relocate entirely if the stand came down. Birds do. Nobody knows where to.

places.hook: Forty years of guano under dead standing timber, worth money, but the colony above will not agree to it.

why.siteAdvantages: The line of a buried gravel ridge that the Dres surveyed and everyone since has simply followed.

why.pressures: It is Dunmer work in a province that reads stone as a moral error, so it is used constantly and spoken of badly; three sections have been let go deliberately.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be let go entirely if the northern holdings emptied. The north would lose its only dry winter road.

why.founding: A small Barsaebic structure built around a single stone socket, with the stone gone. The record cut beside it says it was taken in the same generation the building went up.
why.siteAdvantages: A rock knoll clear of the flood, close enough to the Silyanorn system to be part of it and far enough to be forgotten by everyone working the diggings.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives here. The chamber has been searched exhaustively and there is nothing in it but the socket and the record.
why.pressures: The record beside the socket is legible and says who took the stone, and that name appears nowhere else in any source anyone has consulted.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be the most important room in the north if the stone were put back. The Whispers scholars say so often.

why.founding: Hissmir's Fish Boon Feast needs somewhere to happen that is not the pilgrimage xanmeer, and this river flat below the village has been that place for as long as the feast has existed.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide gravel flat where the river slows: shallow enough to net from the bank, wide enough for the whole village and its pilgrims, and scoured clean by every flood.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here and nothing is built here, because the flood takes it annually and that is understood to be part of the arrangement.
why.pressures: The pilgrim numbers have grown past what the flat can feed, and the Root Stewards will not turn anyone away, so the feast now runs three days instead of one.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would move upstream if the river shifted its channel, which it does about once a century and is due.

hardConstraints: a gravel flat on slow water below Hissmir

why.founding: The Flu began at Stormhold, and the north cordoned itself against its own city. No other line in the province was drawn from the inside out.
why.siteAdvantages: A ring drawn at a day's walk from the city, which on this side puts it up on the rim ground where nothing was farmed anyway.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody occupies it. The vicecanons still pay a marker-walker, and she keeps the cellar swept because she sleeps in it herself four nights a month.
why.pressures: Stormhold has never formally acknowledged that the line was drawn against Stormhold.

hardConstraints: a ring at a day's walk from the city

why.occupantsMotive: Criminals with no ledger and no discipline, most of them three generations out of Blackrose and unable to work anywhere their descent is known.
why.pressures: They cannot resupply and are starting to raid villages they need. That pattern has finished every raw hold before this one.
why.wouldChangeIf: A village retaliation would finish them within a year. The interior tribes have already agreed among themselves which village would lead it.

places.hook: A Blackguard crew living in the ribs of a barge they could not drag back to the water, with one boat and no friends.

places.name: Many-Ways

why.founding: A village that grew as a junction of walkways rather than around a centre.
why.siteAdvantages: Where four routes over soft ground have to meet, because there is nowhere else to put them. The junction is the village's whole capital.
why.occupantsMotive: Walkway-keepers who charge for maintenance and argue about who owes what.
why.pressures: The walkways cost more to keep than the village earns. The keepers have begun charging tolls the tribes using the arms consider extortion.
why.wouldChangeIf: Losing one arm of the junction would strand a whole tribe's route. That tribe has started surveying its own alternative rather than keep paying.

places.hook: Four walkway routes have to meet somewhere. The shrine hung under the deck where they cross is the nearest thing here to a town square.

places.name: The Pulled Field
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in interior swamp (danger band 4), 268 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A grave-pole field where the poles were pulled by looters, raising what they were holding down.
why.siteAdvantages: An old village's burial ground, now cut off from any living village.
why.occupantsMotive: Bog blights and nothing else. The grave-singers send apprentices here to train, quietly.
why.pressures: The poles are still being pulled because the goods under them are real. The looters are heirs of the village that abandoned it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Restaking the field would settle it, and would settle who the grave goods belong to. Nobody local has done it.

places.hook: Looters pulled the grave-poles and what the poles held down got up. The cord and paint still name each one, so you know who is walking at you.

places.name: The Carriers' Rest
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 241 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A staging post on the route by which the bones of Argonians who died away from the Hist are brought back to the dirt.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the river route meets the interior walking route, at the last point a bundle can be re-wrapped and re-labelled before the walk. Under the racks is a cold store cut into the bank, where bundles nobody claimed have been stacked since the office opened.
why.occupantsMotive: Carriers, a recognised profession and a slightly feared one. The family pays them, never the village, so their loyalty is always to the dead.
why.pressures: The 4E produced more distant dead than the route can carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: A backlog is already visible in the racks. A second season of it would force the carriers to choose which families' dead go first, a power no one wants them to have.

places.hook: A freight office for the dead. Racks of wrapped bone wait for a carrier going the right way, and anyone may take work off the delivery board.

why.founding: A xanmeer the forest took: root has replaced stone in about half the structure.
why.siteAdvantages: Nobody defended it and the ground is soft, so the roots won.
why.occupantsMotive: Whatever lives in a warm dry hollow. Twice a year the tenders from the clan-tended meer come to see what stone becoming root looks like.
why.pressures: It is still settling and floors give way. The treasure-hunting outfits price it as unworkable and the tribes have stopped arguing about it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing will change it. It is becoming root, which the restarted-work heretics cite against their own project.

places.hook: Half stone, half root, and one corridor that changes from the one to the other while you are walking down it.

places.name: The Choked Mouth
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 145 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, route; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: An older root tower that fell in and took its line with it.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands on the route it used to serve, so it is still a landmark.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. A shrine at the base gets offerings anyway, left mostly by Waykeepers who will not admit to believing a line can be prayed open.
why.pressures: The line beyond it has been unreachable for a century. The villages it served have reorganised their trade around Helstrom.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the tunnel would reopen the line. Nobody has paid for that work since the villages turned their trade to Helstrom.

places.hook: A fallen rootworm tower lying full length like a felled column, its mouth open at the broken end and going nowhere anyone has come back from.

places.name: The Open Mouth

why.founding: A working rootworm-line exit where the root layer vents to the surface.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise the root tower could push through without flooding.
why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers and the porters who meet the line here. Neither party can price the other out, because neither works without the other.
why.pressures: It is the only exit on this side of the basin and everyone knows it. The Waykeepers' restricted service is the most valuable faction reward in the interior.
why.wouldChangeIf: A collapse would strand the whole eastern line. The fallen tower two days north is what that looks like a century later.

places.hook: A working rootworm exit with a hoist over the mouth and a timetable that is honest about being approximate. Ride it if the Waykeepers will have you.

places.name: Ash-Fence
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 82 m from the nearest route; its choice #3 landform; won on route, landform, region; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: A village burned in the century of uprisings and never rebuilt.
why.siteAdvantages: It stood on the only firm ground on this reach, which is why the burners came. Nobody has been able to leave the ground unused since.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody; a bone-carriers' camp visits.
why.pressures: The neighbouring tribes disagree about who burned it: one says the Legion under Mallicius, one says a rival tribe used the burning as cover.
why.wouldChangeIf: A settled account would let someone rebuild. There is firm ground here for a village of two hundred, in a district with none to spare.

places.hook: Charred pile stumps in a rectangle, with the grave-poles planted inside the burnt footprint rather than outside it, and a root cellar the fire missed.

places.name: The High Root
places.whySiteWon: gorge in rootland deep marsh (danger band 4), 173 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: An aerial root that bridged two hammocks and was made walkable rather than cut down.
why.siteAdvantages: Twenty metres up, over ground that floods completely.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The nearest village maintains the rope line, because the alternative is a half-day round the flooded ground and their fish spoils in that time.
why.pressures: The root is alive and slowly moving. The rope line has been re-rigged three times to follow it.
why.wouldChangeIf: It will eventually be too steep to walk, and everyone knows the year. The village is already arguing about whether to build a walkway instead.

places.hook: A living root walked like a bridge twenty metres above ground that floods completely, with every year's old lashing left hanging beside the new one.

places.name: The Basin Line

why.pressures: The rope is old and there is no way to test it but to use it. The guides price a client's insistence on crossing it accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: Someone re-rigging it would open the route again. It would also put the dead treasure-hunters' camp within a day of the basin guides' shelter.

places.hook: Two ropes over a whitewater reach and an expedition's cache at the far anchor, in a hollow that is not empty.

why.pressures: The route up is easier than the route down. The terrace collects what climbers abandoned rather than carry.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing, unless the tending tribe rules that climbing counts as entering. The heretic-stone dispute could force that ruling.

places.hook: Every ground-level door is sealed, so the only way in is up four terraces and down through a broken roof slab.

why.siteAdvantages: A xanmeer stub bound in root, standing clear of the canopy on its own debris mound. In a region with almost no long sightlines, it is one of the few things that reads at distance.

why.pressures: The debris fan at the base has old falls in it and one from this season. The route was marked, then deliberately unmarked by someone.
why.wouldChangeIf: It will fall. Whether anyone is on it when it does is the open question.

hardConstraints: a debris fan at the base

why.pressures: The nearest village has noticed the traffic and said nothing. The two households who noticed first are being paid.

why.siteAdvantages: A wide shallow basin with a seasonal outlet.
why.occupantsMotive: Scavengers in season, nothing out of it. The same four families come each year and treat the window as inherited property.
why.pressures: The exposure window is short and competitive. Last year two of the families arrived early and drained a channel to widen it.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter cycle would close the window entirely. Four households have built their year around that income.

why.siteAdvantages: Where a hero Hist's roots surface in a hollow and fill it.
why.occupantsMotive: A tender who controls dose and turn, appointed by the tree-minder and answerable to the grove rather than to the users.

why.wouldChangeIf: A crackdown would move it rather than end it. The plant grows in every cold hollow in the district and the hollows are not countable.

why.pressures: The watch is not always posted. The years it lapses are the years the village has men working the porter relay instead.
why.wouldChangeIf: A bridge would solve it, but no one will pay. The four villages that would use it each hold that the crossing benefits the others more.

places.name: The Unmade Work
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 371 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, remote, region.

why.founding: A xanmeer taken apart by its own builders at the Duskfall rather than abandoned.
why.siteAdvantages: The stone was carried away, so what remains is the plan, not the building.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The heretic-stone village quarries it and is condemned for that, but the condemnation has not stopped a single cart.
why.pressures: It is the clearest physical evidence of the renunciation, and the restarted work is quarrying it away.
why.wouldChangeIf: Rebuilding on it would be the loudest possible statement. The Helstrom assembly has avoided visiting for eleven years rather than have to answer one.

places.name: The Interrupted Flight
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 861 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on remote, landform, region; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.mist-locked-hollow-basin (+2.43).

why.founding: Nothing founded it. A man came out of the sky here, at speed, roughly two hundred years after the last one did it near Seyda Neen, and the ground he chose was chosen for him by the wind.
why.siteAdvantages: None. No road, no track, no village within an hour, nothing to bring anyone here and nothing to have seen it.
why.occupantsMotive: He was not going anywhere near here. The letter in his satchel is addressed to a teacher in the tradition and says he has read the great experimenter's notes and corrected the error. The descent, he writes, is the easy part.
why.pressures: Scavengers, water and the season. The satchel is oiled leather and the scrolls in it still work.
why.wouldChangeIf: Somebody finds him and takes the scrolls. The tradition's next student is then the only person left who can fail this way.

places.hook: A man came out of the sky here and did not survive the landing. His scrolls did, and they still work.

why.occupantsMotive: A tribe that has made itself indispensable as the interior's last friendly stop, and charges nothing for water and a great deal for everything else.

places.name: The Roost

why.founding: A dead standing grove that hackwings have used for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: Dead timber with clear flight lines, which is what a roost needs.
why.occupantsMotive: The flock, which has used this grove long enough that the beast-keepers' grandparents complained about the same birds.

places.name: The Turning House
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A rest house kept by the Nisswo on the Helstrom pilgrim road.
why.siteAdvantages: One day's walk from the gate, and deliberately the last stop.
why.occupantsMotive: Nisswo who preach at whoever stops and feed them either way. The feeding is the doctrine's proof; the preaching is the price.
why.pressures: The Hist establishment and the Sithis preachers disagree about the interior's soul, politely. The politeness holds because Helstrom's assembly would have to act if it broke.
why.wouldChangeIf: A closure would leave the last day of the road unsheltered. Pilgrims would arrive at the gate camp instead, and the guides would charge them for it.

places.hook: A Nisswo rest house one day short of the gate, with the sermon painted round the inside of the roof so you read it lying down.

places.name: The Singer's House

why.founding: A grave-singer lives apart from the villages they serve, by custom and by preference.
why.siteAdvantages: Between five villages, on ground none of them claims. None of them will repair the house either.
why.occupantsMotive: A grave-singer and an apprentice who does not want the job.
why.pressures: More staking work since Umbriel than one singer can do. The necropolis village a day away has offered to take the circuit, which the five villages cannot afford.
why.wouldChangeIf: The apprentice leaving would strand five villages' dead. She has family at the Hist-less refuge and has been asking about it.

places.hook: A wall of blank poles and one finished grave-pole by the door that has waited eleven years for a family to come for it.

why.founding: A tree-minder's house, sited by the tree rather than by the village.
why.siteAdvantages: Within sight and earshot of the tree at all times, which the post requires.
why.occupantsMotive: A tree-minder and a second tender who is always present when the first listens. The arrangement costs the grove two adults' labour and is never waived.
why.pressures: The two-tender rule is a direct answer to what exclusive communion did at Lilmoth. The minder here trained under someone who was there.
why.wouldChangeIf: A minder who listened alone would be removed, and the removal would be the district's business within a day.

places.hook: A house built with two of everything to make solitary communion awkward, within earshot of the tree its occupant is not allowed to leave.

places.name: Tsoko Camp

why.founding: The delegation camp used during the convocation month and empty the rest of the year.
why.siteAdvantages: Four hundred metres from the convocation ground, on its landings.
why.occupantsMotive: Delegations, in season. Each brings its own cook, its own water and its own account of why its pitch is where it is.
why.pressures: Precedence disputes about pitch positions are an annual institution. The overflow the nine-trunks village rents has begun to outrank the camp's own back rows.
why.wouldChangeIf: A tribe losing its pitch is a real political event. Two pitches have gone unclaimed for three years without anyone agreeing to reallocate them.

places.hook: Pitch markers cut with tribal signs stand empty eleven months a year. The grass tells you which delegations have stopped coming.

why.founding: A camp for those walking to a hero Hist to grieve.
why.siteAdvantages: The last water before the grove.
why.occupantsMotive: Mourners, in rotation, who mostly do not talk to each other. They leave the camp stocked for the next arrivals, which is the only sociable act of the walk.
why.pressures: Predators have learned that this camp is quiet and slow. The grove will not post a watch, because a watched mourning is not a mourning.
why.wouldChangeIf: A killing here would close the road for a season. The Agaceph grove would then receive its mourners by water, through landings it does not want used.

places.hook: The last water before the grove, with a washing stage and the discarded travel clothes of years hung up as a wall.

places.name: The Counting Tower
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 2), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A ladder tower built to see over the canopy, because nothing else in the interior can.
why.siteAdvantages: The tallest hammock timber for kilometres.
why.occupantsMotive: A watcher on rotation from the nearest village. The job is to count smoke and boats and report both to the naheesh.
why.pressures: From the ground you can see nothing at all. The tower's word is the district's only distant information and is trusted further than it should be.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the tree died the region would lose its only sightline. The vista ledge that would replace it is a day away and closing over.

places.hook: Six ladder stages up one tree to the only place in the region with a horizon, and a slate up there recording what was seen and when.

why.pressures: The tree-minders have put a bounty on them, paid in licence-renewal favour. The licensed stage's own tappers are the ones hunting them.
why.wouldChangeIf: One arrest would name the fence and unroll the trade, including the tapped-tree crew, who use the same buyer under a lapsed concession.

why.founding: A relay yard where interior porters hand off loads between poling stages.
why.siteAdvantages: Where the polable water ends and the walking route begins.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, and a yard-keeper who takes a cut of everything. He holds the only covered store between the water and the walking route.
why.pressures: The yard-keeper's cut is the region's standing grievance. The lizard-steed breeders quote prices that assume it, which makes them complicit.
why.wouldChangeIf: A second yard would break the monopoly. The only firm ground for one belongs to the village that takes the keeper's rent.

why.occupantsMotive: Two caretakers on a rotation nobody envies, drawn by lot from the tribes that fund it, a year each, with no exemption accepted.
why.pressures: Stores are rotated and the register of the one time it was full is read aloud each year. Fewer tribes attend the reading each year.
why.wouldChangeIf: Its use would mean something terrible had happened again. Two funding tribes have quietly let their shares lapse and nobody has announced it.

places.hook: Stores kept for four hundred and eleven people against the day the tribes have to run again, as they did in 4E 48, and still counted.

places.name: The Fallen Nine

why.founding: A trunk root that died and gave way.
why.siteAdvantages: It is on a route people still use, which is why they still dig at it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The bone-carriers come once a year, because four families' dead are under the fall and cannot be recovered to be returned.
why.pressures: The route now goes the long way and costs a day. The porter relay charges for that day and has no interest in seeing the gallery cleared.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing it would restore the route and settle four families' claims. It would also cost the relay yard a quarter of its traffic.

places.hook: A porter train is still under two metres of fallen root with its load, and people are still digging toward it.

places.name: The Severed Branch
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 873 m from the nearest route; its choice #5 landform; won on region, remote, landform; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.hist-heartland.sap-collection-facility-daedric (+1.21).

why.siteAdvantages: Isolated, deep, and directly connected to their target.
why.occupantsMotive: Cultists testing a method, working from notes that came out of the staging camp and going back to it with results.
why.pressures: The tree above is beginning to withdraw and the village does not know why. They have begun consulting a tree-minder who will recognise the pattern.
why.wouldChangeIf: Discovery would move them and lose the notes, which are the only written account of how a severing is actually attempted.

places.name: The Long Throat
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 5), 219 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A single enormous trunk root running toward the basin.
why.siteAdvantages: It is the only dry way toward the deep basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. A guide camp sits at each end, and the two camps keep a tally of who went in so the far end knows who to expect.
why.pressures: Anything that enters behind you cannot be passed. The guides move parties through in one direction only and wait out the day if the tally is wrong.
why.wouldChangeIf: A branch collapse would make it a trap rather than a passage, and would cut the only dry approach to the basin's deep ground.

places.name: The Drowned Stair

why.founding: A root branch that grew downhill into the water table.
why.siteAdvantages: It short-cuts a full day of surface travel for anyone who can hold their breath.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here. Divers pass through, mostly couriers: a message that takes a day by surface takes an afternoon by holding your breath four times.
why.pressures: The water rises in the wet season and drowns the last two landings. Half the year the shortcut is a full dive and the couriers charge double.
why.wouldChangeIf: A dry decade would make it an ordinary road. It would also end a courier trade three villages depend on for news.

places.hook: Flooded steps, each a longer held breath than the last, with the marks of who got how far cut at every landing. It saves a day of surface travel.

places.name: The Underway

why.founding: The trunk root under Helstrom, opened and kept as a road because the surface route is the worst marsh in the province.

why.occupantsMotive: Waykeepers who maintain exactly as far as they are paid to. They post the paid limit in cut marks so nobody can claim not to have known.

why.wouldChangeIf: Losing the Waykeepers would close the interior's only overland link. Helstrom's escorted water traffic could not absorb the difference.

places.name: Sermon Xanmeer

why.founding: A Merethic Sithis temple deliberately left to decay so that its decay could be read aloud as scripture.
why.siteAdvantages: It stands above Glenbridge on the glen's shoulder, so the whole town can watch the sermon progress.
why.occupantsMotive: The Nisswo read it; the Clutch below them sweeps nothing away, because sweeping would be a lie.
why.pressures: The voriplasm-sorcerer Rectavius is sealed in the lowest chamber. The seal is part of the structure being allowed to fail.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become the province's worst problem the day the sermon reaches the bottom course.

places.name: Nine Bells Guar Holding
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in upland hills (danger band 3), 479 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: The Blackwood Road ran on guar bred, broken and rested here. The road trade stopped paying before the herd did.
why.siteAdvantages: Rough grazing too poor for crops and too dry for rice, with nine gates a small band can watch from one spot.
why.occupantsMotive: Sap-poachers keep the pens because stolen guar need somewhere to stand while a brand grows out, same as any other herd.
why.pressures: The bells still ring on schedule. Nobody left to hear them minds.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be raided out within days if Gideon sent more than a token patrol.

places.name: Hangs-Above-The-Water
places.whySiteWon: gorge in upland hills (danger band 3), 128 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: When the Onkobra gorge floods it fills to within a few metres of the rim, so the people who work the gorge live in it: cut chambers and built galleries on the wall, above the worst water and below the wind.
why.siteAdvantages: Dry rock at a constant temperature, on a face nothing can approach without climbing.
why.occupantsMotive: They net the fish the narrows concentrate. Boats that need a hand through the rapid pay for a pilot.
why.pressures: The galleries are reached by ladder and rope. Every year somebody falls. The village argues about cutting a stair, which would also let others up.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would become an ordinary river village the day the stair was cut. So it is never cut.

hardConstraints: a gorge wall above the flood line
places.hook: A village hung on a gorge wall and reached by ladders, forty metres above the water.

places.whySiteWon: firm ground in firm lowland (danger band 4), 174 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A dry rise in the flood plain will always be built on, because for four months a year it is the only ground there is.
why.siteAdvantages: A flood-high knoll that has never gone under in recorded memory, with landing on three sides in the wet.
why.occupantsMotive: In the wet season these households are the flood plain's landlords. In the dry they are its equals.
why.pressures: The rise is small and there is no room to grow. The third generation is having to leave.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned within a year of a flood that topped it.

hardConstraints: a rise that has never flooded

places.name: Ladder-To-The-Light
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in rootland deep marsh (danger band 5), 43 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on route, nearPoint, landform; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-3/4'.

why.founding: The fig canopy over the lower Onkobra is closed enough that a fringe village cannot see its own river. A stack of platforms and ladders was built to put a lookout above the leaves. People found other uses for being up there.
why.siteAdvantages: A single very old fig with a straight bole, standing on firm ground within sight of the road, tall enough to break the canopy by six metres.
why.occupantsMotive: A lookout is paid by three villages to sit up there in the flood season and watch which lanes are open; the rest of the year it is climbed by anyone who wants to.
why.pressures: Every platform is younger than the one below it, so the bottom ladder is the oldest thing here. The tree is growing out of the fixings.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be abandoned the moment the tree died. There is no second tree of this height within two kilometres.

hardConstraints: a canopy-breaking tree on firm ground
in the fringe country, not the marsh interior
places.hook: A stack of platforms up one old fig. From the top you can see where the river goes.

places.name: Long Causeway
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in lake & standing water (danger band 2), 110 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #4 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A lashed-log causeway built by the villages on driven piles, low enough that a flood runs over it instead of taking it away. The Imperial answer to the same water was an embankment.
why.siteAdvantages: Crosses the widest shallow between the Gideon hinterland and the marsh edge, where the bottom will take a pile but no bank will hold.
why.occupantsMotive: Six villages own segments and each maintains its own, so the causeway's quality changes every two hundred metres.
why.pressures: One village's segment is always in dispute and therefore always the worst.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would be replaced piecemeal forever.

hardConstraints: a bottom that will take driven piles
places.hook: A log road laid across the shallows on piles. In the wet months it is the only way east that is not swimming.

why.siteAdvantages: Above the fever line and above the flood. The water is clean and the nights are cold enough to keep grain.
why.occupantsMotive: Terrace farmers who can sell dry grain into a province that mostly cannot grow any, at a price that justifies carrying it down a mountain.
why.pressures: Everything has to be carried up. In the dry months the shelf has only the water it stores. Gideon's assessors tax upland grain as a luxury.
why.wouldChangeIf: Would empty in one generation if the cisterns failed. They are the oldest Imperial thing here.

hardConstraints: upland shelf above the flood and the fever line
stored water for the dry months
places.hook: The one village in the fringe above both the fever line and the flood, where an outlander sleeps well.

why.founding: The Second Empire tried to make the Onkobra navigable to the uplands with a staircase of stone locks.
why.siteAdvantages: At the reach where the river drops fastest.

why.founding: Argonians raised outside a Hist's reach built a hearth ring here, on the one ground where their gloor-faded skin drew no comment.
why.siteAdvantages: Close enough to Gideon for work, far enough that nobody had to explain themselves twice a day.
why.occupantsMotive: They rebuilt a mile off when the old ring flooded twice in one year and left the first houses standing rather than pull them down.
why.pressures: The new settlement will not send anyone back for the timber. Nobody wants to say why.

why.pressures: The Sul-Xan raid camp sits on the ruin the Ca-Uxith are sworn to keep. The tribe has no means to remove them. The geyser field is getting louder. The elders disagree about whose fault that is.

places.name: Blackrose
places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'blackrose' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: Built by the Lilmothiit in a lake where three rivers converge; rebuilt by the Empire after 1E 2837 and held since by whoever holds the island core.
why.siteAdvantages: The hinge of the south: Murkwood's water from the north-east, Oliis Bay from the south, eastern Blackwood from the west, and Bramman's concealed river out to Topal Bay. The lake is a wide fringe marsh with a hard island in it. The island is the city.
why.occupantsMotive: Toll and transit revenue, and whatever comes out of the Rose. The city keeps whoever does not leave.
why.pressures: It raised an army against the Third Empire and watched a battlemage break it with one spell. It distrusts magic first and outsiders second.

places.name: Deepmire, the Refuge
places.whySiteWon: flood high in interior swamp (danger band 4), 568 m from the nearest route; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; landform wishes taken from the type recipe (record had none).

why.founding: The shelter of last resort. An all-but-inaccessible plateau in the north-north-east that even the tribes avoid, where the presence of Sithis is strong, holding pre-Duskfall xanmeers and the skeletons of swamp leviathans. Nobody goes there except to shelter, and a caretaker few tend it.
why.siteAdvantages: High, dry, defensible ground in a province that has almost none, with one approach that can be walked and no approach that can be poled.
why.occupantsMotive: The caretakers do not live here so much as keep it fit to be lived in. Stores turned, shelters re-roofed, against a need they hope never comes.
why.pressures: In 4E 48 the need did come: Murkmire's survivors fled up onto the plateau while Umbriel passed overhead, and the caretakers have been feeding that memory ever since. The Umbriel Witness Society wants the memorial catalogued, the Nisswo want it let go, and the caretakers want it left exactly as it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the argument over the memorial is settled by anyone but the caretakers, the plateau stops being a refuge and becomes a destination.

hardConstraints: upland ground above the flood by 40m+
places.hook: The last dry ground in the province, kept ready for a night that has not come again. You may shelter here, but you may not stay.

places.whySiteWon: Owner-approved settlement anchor 'archon' (world/sources/anchors, Phase 2 gate); position kept exactly.

why.founding: A deep, sheltered estuary mouth on the Padomaic was the one place on this coast a foreign hull could lie safely, so the Second Empire and then the East Empire Company built a stone quay here. The Saxhleel town grew landward of it.
why.siteAdvantages: Estuary with a landable stone shore, a river road into the interior, and the only stretch of the east coast where the mangrove wall breaks for more than a kilometre.
why.occupantsMotive: An Argonian-majority harbour population who work the water as amphibians and run the port authority out of dead Company offices, alongside state customs and a long-settled Dunmer merchant minority from the Morrowind trade.
why.pressures: The lawful port is the province's only functioning customs choke, so everything that wants to avoid it goes round it: half-chartered hulls land on the Oliis shore and wreckers work the Padomaic beaches south of the city. The mangrove behind the city is D4 within a kilometre of the gate. Nobody in the harbour authority will discuss the sealed Shadowscale sanctuary.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the Archon-Lilmoth-Soulrest-Tear line stopped running, or if the harbour authority lost its claim to the Company buildings, Archon would become a large fishing town in a month.

hardConstraints: deep water at the quay line at the highest seasonal level
places.hook: The one harbour on this coast where a foreign hull can tie up legally. The customs desk will also tell you where a cargo went.

places.name: Shows-The-Wrong-Light
places.whySiteWon: cove in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 498 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, bound, sightline.

why.founding: Archon is the only lawful landing on this coast, so a hull that misses the estuary in weather looks for any light it can see. A shore gang worked out what a light in the wrong place is worth.
why.siteAdvantages: A shelving beach south of the estuary with a bar offshore and no settlement within sight of the fire.
why.occupantsMotive: Landless coast households who lost their fishing ground and found that a cargo comes ashore whether or not the crew does.
why.pressures: The harbour authority knows the beach exists, but cannot prove which fire is which; the pilots of Portdun Mont lose a hull a season to it and want it burnt out.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the estuary marks were kept properly lit the gang would have nothing to imitate. They would go back to fishing, or go to Alten Corimont.

hardConstraints: a shelving beach a laden hull can ground on
no settlement in line of sight of the fire
places.hook: The light on this beach is not the estuary light. The cargo stacked behind it came off the last hull that thought otherwise.

npcs: boss · D3 · single · named — the fire-keeper; the only one here who knows where the cargo goes
rank-and-file · D2 · band — shore gang, armed with what they took off hulls
captive · D0 · pair — survivors off the last wreck, kept because drowning them is work
loot: wreck-cargo · loot-cache · tier-3 · off a hull that never reached Archon customs
ledger-or-document · evidence · tier-3 · a tally naming who buys the cargo in the city

places.name: The Counted Lots
places.whySiteWon: cove in ocean (danger band 0), 434 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'spacing-1/2'.

why.founding: An amphibious people with a port to sell into will work a pearl bed, and the bed becomes property the moment it is worth money.
why.siteAdvantages: Clear water over a firm bed inside the reef, six to twelve metres — deeper than an outsider can casually work.
why.occupantsMotive: Diver families holding numbered lots by inheritance, with a surface tender each.
why.pressures: The deep lots pay best and kill divers; the tally book records both facts on the same page.
why.wouldChangeIf: If foreigners learned to dive here the lot system collapses, which is why nobody teaches them.

hardConstraints: clear water over a worked bed
places.hook: Numbered pearl lots held by inheritance, with a tally book that records the drownings as well as the takings.

npcs: crew · D1 · few — 2-6 D1 divers
rank-and-file · few — one surface tender
loot: unique-item · unique-item · tier-3
workshop-stock · materials · tier-3

places.name: Portdun Mont
places.whySiteWon: flood high in mangrove forest (danger band 2), 229 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: The village grew on the rise behind the pilots' watch, above the beach landing and below the ridge line.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm ground above the flood, a clear view down the whole estuary approach, and a beach landing at the foot of the stair.
why.occupantsMotive: Pilot families who take fees to bring hulls in, and who remember when the fee was collected differently.
why.pressures: Archon's authority stops at the headland; the pilots' monopoly is customary rather than legal. The anchorage below the cliff has a past.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the harbour authority licensed its own pilots, Portdun Mont would be a fishing hamlet in a year.

hardConstraints: a bench above water with a landing below
places.hook: Every hull bound for Archon takes a pilot here first, so the village hears the coast's news before the city does.

npcs: crew · D2 · band — pilot families; the trade is hereditary and closed
named-keeper · D2 · single · named — the headman, who decides which hulls get a pilot and which wait

places.interiorScope: settlement: about 3–8 structures, every one enterable; the block below is the principal interior

places.name: Keeps-Its-Own-Cordon
places.whySiteWon: land bridge in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 2), 163 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; won on bound, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A village put under cordon during a later outbreak and never formally released, because the order that would release it was never written.
why.siteAdvantages: An island in the lagoon with one landing, which made it the obvious place to put people.
why.occupantsMotive: Descendants of the quarantined, who have been free to leave for a century and have not.
why.pressures: They are healthy, they are not confined, and they behave as if they are.
why.wouldChangeIf: If somebody produced a release order — real or forged — the whole arrangement would have to end.

hardConstraints: an island or a single-landing site
places.hook: A cordon nobody has enforced for a century, kept by the people inside it.

npcs: family · D1 · few — D1 households
loot: ledger-or-document · lore-fragment · tier-3

places.name: The Three Tongues
places.whySiteWon: river mouth in tidal delta (danger band 2), 62 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, route, region.

why.founding: A port needs paid lodging with a fire, a bed and a room full of people who know things.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quay front, one door from the mooring line.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who trades in information as her actual business.
why.pressures: Two of the three languages spoken in the front room are lying.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the port trade fell away this becomes a village inn and the coast's news is traded somewhere else.

hardConstraints: on a route with a landing
places.hook: Three languages in one room, a contract board on the wall, and a keeper whose actual trade is what she overhears.

npcs: named-keeper · D1 · single · named — the keeper; sells rooms, trades information
crew · D2 · band — boat crews off the Oliis and Padomaic runs

places.name: Seafalls
places.whySiteWon: water narrows in tropical jungle (danger band 2), 172 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, danger.

why.founding: A drop in the river stops laden hulls dead, so everything going inland is unloaded, carried past the fall and loaded again. A town grew on the carry.
why.siteAdvantages: The furthest point upriver a laden boat can reach, with landings above and below the drop and firm ground between them.
why.occupantsMotive: Porters, transfer clerks and hauliers whose entire livelihood is that the falls exist.
why.pressures: The navigable limit moves with the season and this year's board does not match last year's; the porters price accordingly.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the portage slipway above the falls were ever mechanised, the town's whole labour economy evaporates.

hardConstraints: landings above and below the drop
places.hook: Everything going inland is carried past the fall on somebody's back. The porters know what is in every load.

npcs: crew · D1 · band — porters working the carry, paid by the load
official · D2 · few — transfer clerks who reconcile what went up against what came down
merchant · D1 · few — factors buying inland cargo before it reaches Archon customs

places.name: Seven-Terrace
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 4), 565 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, remote; placed from the homeless batch at stage 'neighbour-zone'.

why.founding: Deliberately closed by its own people, with its traps live and its vakka-stone mechanisms intact.
why.siteAdvantages: Seven terraces of dressed stone standing in D4 jungle with no tending path to them, which is why nobody reopened it.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing living; the traps still work.
why.pressures: The tending clan a valley away knows the door and will not open it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If it were opened, whatever it was closed against becomes everyone's problem.

places.hook: Seven terraces of climbable wall, with a trapdoor on the top one.

creatures: something-old · D4 · single · on on-interact — sealed under the top terrace, and sealed from the inside

places.name: Haj-Mota Wallow
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in coastal lagoon & salt marsh (danger band 3), 422 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.archon-glowgill-byre (+1.14).

why.founding: The animals that supply the shell trade live where the mud is deep and the water shallow.
why.siteAdvantages: Churned shallow mud at the delta edge, warm and food-rich.
why.occupantsMotive: A small number of very large animals and one abandoned set of cutter's tools.
why.pressures: The yard needs them, but the villages want them cleared.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the wallow were worked out the shell yard closes and the district's shields become imports.

places.hook: A haj-mota wallow at the delta edge: shell, bone and eggs, guarded by the thing that made the mud.

creatures: apex-ambusher · D3 · single · on on-approach — the resident haj-mota; it surfaces under you
scavenger · D2 · few · on on-noise — mud-scavengers working the last kill
loot: workshop-stock · materials · tier-2

places.name: Climbs-The-Long-Back
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 32 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #2 landform; won on route, landform, region.

why.founding: A village built along a shelf above the flood line, until the spring above it gave way in a wet season and took the timber retaining walls down the slope with it.
why.siteAdvantages: Drained firm ground with a spring head above it and one approach that four people could hold, now unheld.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody keeps the terraces now. A pack has taken the lower platforms where the households used to trade.
why.pressures: The retaining walls keep failing and taking more of the slope with each wet season.
why.wouldChangeIf: Rebuilding the spring channel could resettle the lower terraces, but the collapse is getting worse each year.

places.hook: A terrace village that slid down its own hillside when the spring failed, now home to whatever moved into the broken platforms.

loot: personal-effects · loot-cache · tier-2 · left by the people who lived here
hidden-cache · gear · tier-3 · whatever the current occupants have taken

places.name: The Two-Hour Flat
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 33 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its choice #3 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland.

why.founding: A delta flat that shortens the coast journey and is crossable only while the basin's tidal amplitude leaves it dry. In practice that is a short morning.
why.siteAdvantages: Firm sand under shallow water at low tide, marked by a stake line laid generations ago.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives on it; six people are usually waiting at the head.
why.pressures: The tide does not negotiate and the window is never the same length twice.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a causeway were ever built here, the whole district's travel times change and the shelter dies.

hardConstraints: firm bed under the marked line
places.hook: Two hours of firm sand twice a day; miss the window and the crossing is a swim in a running channel.

places.name: The Tide Streets
places.whySiteWon: shallow marsh in mangrove forest (danger band 3), 38 m from the nearest route; at the water's edge; its first-choice landform; won on landform, region, submerged.

why.founding: A stilt village on subsiding delta ground that the water took street by street over sixty years, until the last households moved to the rise behind it.
why.siteAdvantages: Shallow clear water over an intact street plan, readable from a boat at low tide.
why.occupantsMotive: Salvagers above; nothing below but what the salvagers cannot reach.
why.pressures: It has been picked over for a century and the deep streets still have not been worked.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the delta shifted again, the whole plan silts over and the salvage trade here ends.

hardConstraints: submerged street plan legible from above
places.hook: A whole street plan under clear shallow water, with the deep end of it still unworked.

npcs: rank-and-file · D2 · few — 0-4 D2 salvagers above
loot: hidden-cache · loot-cache · tier-3
ledger-or-document · lore-fragment · tier-3

places.name: Four-Eight
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in fringe marsh (danger band 3), 154 m from the nearest route; no free 'flood-high' site was left in the zone, so plain ground; won on route, region, hinterland.

why.founding: Umbriel crossed this coast in 4E 48 and the bodies it left had to go somewhere the Hist could not be blamed for.
why.siteAdvantages: A tidal flat above the village line where the ground could be opened quickly and in quantity.
why.occupantsMotive: Bone-carriers still call here on the way south; nobody else does.
why.pressures: The dead here were stripped, so there is nothing to repatriate.
why.wouldChangeIf: If a way were found to return even one of them, the Umbriel Witness Society gains its first real relic.

hardConstraints: ground that can be opened in quantity
places.hook: A grave mound longer than the village that dug it, with no name on it and a cut in the ground you can still open.

creatures: something-old · D2 · few · on on-interact — what Umbriel left behind in the ones it did not finish with
loot: grave-goods · loot-cache · tier-2

places.name: Still-Water Sleeping-Tree
places.whySiteWon: firm ground in tropical jungle (danger band 3), 472 m from the nearest route; its choice #2 landform; won on landform, region, hinterland; site exchanged in the swap pass with place.saxhleel-coast.estuary-keepers-lodge (+2.09).

why.founding: The Hist opened a break in the canopy on a firm rise at the marsh edge and the village that answered it stood there for generations.
why.siteAdvantages: A firm rise where the fringe marsh met the jungle wall, with fresh water and a canopy break the Hist made itself.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody lives here now. Still water rose over the sleeping tree and the xanmeer beneath it and never went back down.
why.pressures: Something old holds the drowned chamber under the tree and a guardian keeps watch over what is left of it.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the water ever drained, the tree and the xanmeer beneath it would be exposed for the first time in living memory.

hardConstraints: a living Hist with a canopy break
places.hook: The village's sleeping Hist and the xanmeer beneath it went under still water and never came back up and something is still down there.
